findings.body: Both branches of the helper return false, so `IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` has no effect: SQL expressions are rejected with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" even when the feature flag is explicitly enabled. Additionally the variable `enabled` is assigned the negation of the flag, so it is true exactly when the feature is disabled, making the code actively misleading.
findings.failure_mode: The feature toggle silently has no effect and future readers/maintainers are misled by inverted, dead branching, causing incorrect gating behavior for flag-enabled deployments.
findings.impact: Both branches of the helper return false, so `IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` has no effect: SQL expressions are rejected with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" even when the feature flag is explicitly enabled. Additionally the variable `enabled` is assigned the negation of the flag, so it is true exactly when the feature is disabled, making the code actively misleading.
findings.root_cause: The newly added helper inverts the feature-flag result into a variable misleadingly named `enabled` and returns false on both branches, so the flag lookup is dead code.
findings.suggested_fix: If the flag is meant to gate the feature, replace the helper body with `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (and make it a method on *ExpressionQueryReader). If SQL expressions are meant to be unconditionally disabled for the security fix, delete the flag check and the helper and return the error directly in the QueryTypeSQL case.
findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, making the FlagSqlExpressions feature-toggle check dead code
findings.trigger: An administrator enables the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle and submits an expression query with type "sql" through the expression-parser path (ReadQuery via buildCMDNode with FlagExpressionParser on).
findings.verifier_reason: The patch adds lines 194-200 verbatim: `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` followed by `if enabled { return false } return false`. Both branches return false, making the feature flag check dead code. The trigger (enabling FlagSqlExpressions and submitting a SQL expression query via ReadQuery) is realistic, and the impact (flag has no effect, SQL expressions always rejected) follows directly from the code.

pr.body:
<!--

Thank you for sending a pull request! Here are some tips:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contribution guide at https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

2. Ensure you include and run the appropriate tests as part of your Pull Request.

3. In a new feature or configuration option, an update to the documentation is necessary. Everything related to the documentation is under the docs folder in the root of the repository.

4. If the Pull Request is a work in progress, make use of GitHub's "Draft PR" feature and mark it as such.

5. If you can not merge your Pull Request due to a merge conflict, Rebase it. This gets it in sync with the main branch.

6. Name your PR as "<FeatureArea>: Describe your change", e.g. Alerting: Prevent race condition. If it's a fix or feature relevant for the changelog describe the user impact in the title. The PR title is used to auto-generate the changelog for issues marked with the "add to changelog" label.

7. If your PR content should be added to the What's New document for the next major or minor release, add the **add to what's new** label to your PR. Note that you should add this label to the main PR that introduces the feature; do not add this label to smaller PRs for the feature.

-->

**What is this feature?**

Remove reference to DuckDB

**Why do we need this feature?**

See the blog post describing the vulnerability, for which a fix was rolled out to all Grafana versions earlier today:
https://grafana.com/blog/2024/10/17/grafana-security-release-critical-severity-fix-for-cve-2024-9264/

The full extent of our documentation around this feature seems to be here:
https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/81666/files#diff-16fb71b28e5b6197615abba8a07bc73d9bf75ebc60311663e1c29976de5cc9a6

All we've documented is that the feature-flag exists. That flag still exists in the codebase, so I'm tempted not to touch that documentation for now. We can always follow up with more improvements after this PR.

**Who is this feature for?**

Everyone

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

This moves the security fix into Grafana repo itself, now that it has been publicly announced. We need this here so we can clean up and simplify our Security-releases pipeline once again.

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
   Behaviour of this patch was already verified manually by @toddtreece. See his confirmation of this on our private slack, [here](https://raintank-corp.slack.com/archives/C07P60RBAUD/p1727902629844259?thread_ts=1727901896.911799&cid=C07P60RBAUD)
   Tested again on the Ephemeral instance here: https://ephemeral1511182194942samjewe.grafana-dev.net/d/be18gem24w2dcf/test-sql-expressions-bugfix?from=now-1h&to=now&timezone=browser
- [ ] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [ ] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-whats-new), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/) doc.
pr.title: ServerSideExpressions: Disable SQL Expressions to prevent RCE and LFI vulnerability

raw_findings.body: Both branches of the helper return false, so `IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` has no effect: SQL expressions are rejected with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" even when the feature flag is explicitly enabled. Additionally the variable `enabled` is assigned the negation of the flag, so it is true exactly when the feature is disabled, making the code actively misleading.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The feature toggle silently has no effect and future readers/maintainers are misled by inverted, dead branching, causing incorrect gating behavior for flag-enabled deployments.
raw_findings.impact: Both branches of the helper return false, so `IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` has no effect: SQL expressions are rejected with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" even when the feature flag is explicitly enabled. Additionally the variable `enabled` is assigned the negation of the flag, so it is true exactly when the feature is disabled, making the code actively misleading.
raw_findings.root_cause: The newly added helper inverts the feature-flag result into a variable misleadingly named `enabled` and returns false on both branches, so the flag lookup is dead code.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: If the flag is meant to gate the feature, replace the helper body with `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (and make it a method on *ExpressionQueryReader). If SQL expressions are meant to be unconditionally disabled for the security fix, delete the flag check and the helper and return the error directly in the QueryTypeSQL case.
raw_findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, making the FlagSqlExpressions feature-toggle check dead code
raw_findings.trigger: An administrator enables the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle and submits an expression query with type "sql" through the expression-parser path (ReadQuery via buildCMDNode with FlagExpressionParser on).

raw_findings.body: The security-motivated behavior change (rejecting SQL expressions in ReadQuery) is unverified; the dead/inverted logic in enableSqlExpressions ships undetected, and a future regression that re-enables SQL expressions would not be caught by CI.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Review and CI cannot verify the intended disablement semantics, allowing the inverted helper logic and any future regression to pass unnoticed.
raw_findings.impact: The security-motivated behavior change (rejecting SQL expressions in ReadQuery) is unverified; the dead/inverted logic in enableSqlExpressions ships undetected, and a future regression that re-enables SQL expressions would not be caught by CI.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch introduces new security-critical gating logic for QueryTypeSQL without adding any test that exercises it.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add ReadQuery test cases for `"type": "sql"` asserting the returned error, covering both `featuremgmt.WithFeatures()` and `featuremgmt.WithFeatures(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` to pin the intended gating behavior.
raw_findings.title: New QueryTypeSQL rejection path in ReadQuery has no test coverage
raw_findings.trigger: Running the existing pkg/expr test suite: pkg/expr/reader_test.go only exercises reduce queries, and pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go tests are all t.Skip()'d, so no test executes the new QueryTypeSQL gate with the flag enabled or disabled.

finding.trigger: Running the existing pkg/expr test suite: pkg/expr/reader_test.go only exercises reduce queries, and pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go tests are all t.Skip()'d, so no test executes the new QueryTypeSQL gate with the flag enabled or disabled.
finding.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage gap observation, not a defect introduced by the patch. The claim that tests are missing is a quality concern but does not identify a concrete bug with a trigger and observable failure caused by the changed code. Absence of tests is not itself a defect in the production code.
